enonce_intro_markdown: The probability that a student passes in the first sequence examination is $\dfrac35$ and passes in the second sequence examination is $\dfrac{9}{10}$. Find the probability that the student:
incertitudes: Q15 : l'indépendance des deux examens n'est pas dite dans le sujet ; elle est supposée en (b) (produit des probabilités).

questions.corrige_markdown:
Failing is the complement of passing: $P(\text{fails first})=1-\dfrac35=\dfrac25$.

**Probability $=\dfrac25$ (that is $0.4$).**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) passes in both sequences. *[4 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Assuming the two examinations are independent, multiply the probabilities:

$P(\text{passes both})=\dfrac35\times\dfrac9{10}=\dfrac{27}{50}$.

**Probability $=\dfrac{27}{50}$ (that is $0.54$).**
